label: input token u in the original phase (position >= 3)
explanation: Token detector for u. It fires when u is input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 3 or later, and in_tok=u accounts for 99.9% of activation mass. It is silent at t=0-1, nearly silent at t=2, and silent on <DEL> and on u fed back during the copy phase. The top examples (about 2.7) are u at t=5 in sequences starting with x/i; the weakest are u at t=3-4. False positives are mostly u at t=3. Other tokens produce only tiny residual activations.

issues: The core claims hold. 99.9% of activation mass is on in_tok=u. The feature is silent at t=0-1, has 49 activations at t=2, never fires on <DEL>, and fires only 50 times in the copy phase. Test scores reproduce: P 0.941, R 0.986, F1 0.963, mass recall 0.998.

The false positives are not scattered noise; they form one systematic class. They are u at t=3, and whether the feature fires there depends on the first token orig(0). Precision of u&t==3 is only 0.82 overall. By orig(0) it is: p 0.10, y 0.18, k 0.25, a 0.35, j 0.48, 1 0.51, b 0.62, t 0.66, z 0.68. For c, d, e, g, h, i, l, n, o, u, v, w, x, 2 and 3 it is 1.0.
At t>=4 the predicate is nearly clean (precision 0.989). So the claim that the feature fires on u 'at position 3 or later' overclaims for t=3: there it is gated by the sequence's first token.

Excluding t==3 & orig(0) in {a,p,y,k,j,1} raises test precision to 0.979 and F1 to 0.974, with recall at 0.969. The gap is real but affects only weak activations, so the main token-detector reading still holds.
skeptic.revised_label: input token u in the original phase (t >= 3); at t=3 it is suppressed when the first token is p/y/k/a/j/1
